categories.main_business_segments: FOX operates through two primary reportable segments: Cable Network Programming and Television. Cable Network Programming includes FOX News Media, FOX Sports, and related cable channels, while the Television segment encompasses the FOX broadcast network, Tubi (AVOD streaming), 29 owned and operated local TV stations, and various production companies. Additional operations include Credible (a consumer finance marketplace) and the FOX Studio Lot, which are reported under Corporate and Other.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: FOX leverages advanced broadcast and digital distribution technologies, including traditional cable/satellite (MVPDs), virtual MVPDs, and direct-to-consumer streaming platforms. The company produces original news, sports, and entertainment content through in-house studios (e.g., FOX Entertainment Studios, Bento Box Entertainment) and co-productions, and distributes content via authenticated streaming apps, AVOD (Tubi), SVOD (FOX Nation), and FAST channels. FOX is also investing in ATSC 3.0 'NextGenTV' broadcast standards and digital advertising technologies.
categories.primary_customers_markets: FOX primarily serves U.S. households, advertisers, and content distributors (MVPDs, virtual MVPDs, and digital platforms). Key customer groups include national and local advertisers, cable/satellite operators, streaming audiences (notably younger, diverse, and 'cord-cutter' demographics via Tubi), and financial product consumers through Credible. Major end markets are news, sports, entertainment, and digital media.
categories.geographic_coverage: FOX's operations are predominantly U.S.-focused, with national reach through cable networks, the FOX broadcast network, and local TV stations covering 18 DMAs (including 14 of the top 15 U.S. markets). Tubi and select digital offerings extend to some international regions. The FOX Studio Lot is based in Los Angeles, and the company holds equity interests in international ventures such as Flutter Entertainment.
categories.supply_chain_position: FOX operates at the downstream end of the media supply chain, focusing on content creation, aggregation, and direct distribution to consumers and advertisers. It controls both production (via studios and in-house teams) and distribution (broadcast, cable, digital streaming, and local stations), with some upstream integration through content licensing and co-productions.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: FOX's strategic priorities include maintaining leadership in live news, sports, and entertainment; expanding digital distribution and direct-to-consumer engagement (notably through Tubi and the upcoming FOX One streaming service); and investing in original content and technology. The company is focused on innovation in advertising, multiplatform measurement, and leveraging data-driven digital platforms, while optimizing its sports rights portfolio and expanding in-house production capabilities.
categories.revenue_model: FOX generates revenue primarily through affiliate fees from content distributors (47% of FY25 revenue), advertising sales (42%), and other sources such as content licensing, production services, and digital marketplaces (11%). Advertising is sold across linear TV, digital platforms, and AVOD/FAST channels, while affiliate fees are derived from MVPDs, virtual MVPDs, and retransmission consent agreements. Additional revenue streams include studio rentals and financial product commissions via Credible.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: FOX competes with major broadcast networks (ABC, NBC, CBS), cable news and sports networks (CNN, MSNBC, ESPN, TNT, TBS), streaming platforms (Netflix, Amazon Prime Video, Hulu, YouTube, Peacock, Apple TV+), and digital media companies. FOX News leads in cable news ratings, FOX Sports holds marquee sports rights, and Tubi is among the fastest-growing AVOD services. The company positions itself as a leader in live, appointment-based programming and premium brands.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: In fiscal 2025, FOX generated $16.3 billion in revenue (up 17% year-over-year), with net income attributable to stockholders of $2.26 billion (up 51%). Adjusted EBITDA was $3.62 billion, and the company ended the year with $5.4 billion in cash and cash equivalents. FOX maintains a strong balance sheet, significant liquidity, and a history of returning capital to shareholders through dividends and stock repurchases.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: FOX emphasizes its leadership in live, premium news, sports, and entertainment content, delivered through culturally significant brands (FOX News, FOX Sports, Tubi, FOX Entertainment). The company differentiates itself with appointment-based programming, broad national and local reach, and a strong digital presence targeting younger, diverse audiences. Its ability to deliver large, engaged audiences at scale and innovative advertising solutions is a key value proposition for advertisers and distributors.
